[PATH:empirical] Controlled experiments comparing LLM performance on out-of-distribution reasoning tasks (e.g., compositional generalization benchmarks like SCAN or COGS) across multiple scales, with systematic measurement of reasoning failures that persist beyond scaling trends — Directly tests whether scaling overcomes fundamental reasoning limitations; persistent failures at large scales would support the hypothesis, while convergence to human-level performance would refute it.

[PATH:theoretical] Theoretical analysis of autoregressive transformer capacity to implement algorithmic reasoning, e.g., using circuit complexity or formal language theory to prove lower bounds on what next-token prediction can compute (e.g., inability to simulate Turing machines beyond finite memory or to handle unbounded recursion) — Provides formal grounding for architectural limitations that scaling cannot circumvent, distinguishing between empirical scaling trends and inherent computational constraints.

[PATH:literature] Survey and meta-analysis of recent literature on emergent reasoning abilities in LLMs (e.g., chain-of-thought, tool use, self-consistency) to assess whether these methods bypass the next-token prediction bottleneck or merely mask it — Evaluates whether current architectural modifications or prompting strategies address the hypothesized limitation, or if fundamental barriers remain even with advanced techniques.
